entries.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 15 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about a thousand words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, what brought you to HD recently?
Videos on YouTube.
Got it — YouTube videos. Which video, or which creator?
The hobbyist miner.
Nice — the Hobbyist Miner. Do you remember what he was covering in the video that pulled you over to HD?
I'm interested in the new l one and the lottery Bitcoin miners as well as the Dogecoin.
Got it — the lottery Bitcoin miners and a Dogecoin one too. Let me pull up the lottery side first. Have you seen this one — the NerdQaxe Rev 6.1?
Yes. I have.
What did you think of it?
It's something I'm looking for, possibly something double. The hash rate.
Interesting — you'd want roughly double the hashrate. Why double specifically?
Just to grade in my odds. On hitting a block
Makes sense — better odds at a block. So is this for the lottery thrill, or are you thinking about it more seriously than that?
Basically, a lottery ticket. See if I can hit
Got it — a lottery ticket shot. When you picture actually hitting a block on one of these — what does that moment look like for you? Like, what would you do?
Excitement. Probably by a another house.

Ha — buy another house. That's a real answer. So this is genuinely "change my life" money in your head, not just a fun number on a screen.

Have you bought any miner before, or would the NerdQaxe be your first?
First. No. I've bought in many miners before.
Got it — you've bought many miners before. Where'd you buy those from?
Secondhand Bitmain Ice River.
Bitmain secondhand and Ice River — okay. So you've actually run gear before. What made you land on HD this time instead of going secondhand again?
I prefer brand new. That way I know it's brand new out of the box It's got a little bit of a warranty, but more importantly, it works.
That makes sense — brand new, warranty, and you know it works. Has that bitten you before? Like, did a secondhand unit show up dead or flake out on you?
No. It hasn't. Just a little bit of dirt. So I had to clean. The insides and the outside of the miners.
Right — cleaning dirt out of secondhand gear. Annoying but not a dealbreaker. So if secondhand has actually worked fine for you, what tipped you to brand new THIS time specifically?
Newer miners, and being as a lottery, I just wanna pull it out of the box.

Got it — newer silicon, and you just want to plug it in. That actually connects to something I wanted to ask — when you say "newer miners," are you tracking specific chips, like waiting for a particular next-gen release?
No. Not really.

Okay, fair — not chasing a specific chip. Let me show you the Dogecoin side since you mentioned that too. Actually — have you seen the bundle? It pairs the NerdQaxe with a Bitaxe Gamma and a Hammer miner (that one does Doge/Litecoin via scrypt). Have you come across this?
I've seen it. But I'm looking for a little bit higher hash rate around ten to twelve t h for BTC.
Got it — 10 to 12 TH/s on the BTC side specifically. That's roughly double the NerdQaxe. Have you found anything in that range you're eyeing — here or elsewhere?

Uh, I found it here. It's the nerd octox. Twelve ferrahash There's also the Nexus s one in the ten terahash range. I'm willing to buy a six terra hash if the price was good. I could double up and have twelve, but it looks like it's easier and cheaper just to go with the nerd octoax.

That's really useful — so you've actually done the math: two NerdQaxe Rev 6.1s at $249 each is $498 for 12 TH/s, versus one NerdOctaxe at 12 TH/s. What's making the single Octaxe feel easier or cheaper to you?

Less space. One power supply, Probably for shipping purposes, could possibly be cheaper. But I'm willing if there is a package that would get it down under the twelve terahash. Say, uh, four forty something like that. Something where I'm saving a little bit of money I would entertain the idea of buying two instead of the one twelve tera hash.

Got it — so if HD bundled two 6 TH/s NerdQaxes around $440-ish, you'd actually flip and take the pair over the single Octaxe. Less space and one PSU is the appeal of the single, but price would override it.

You also mentioned the Nexus at 10 TH/s — where'd you see that one?
I've seen it on your your website here, the Nexus s one exclusive. It's, uh, six hundred and fifty dollars, so it's a little bit higher than I've really wanted to pay.
Got it — $650 on the Nexus S1 feels above where you want to land. What's the number in your head — like, what would you actually be willing to spend to get into the 10-12 TH/s range?
To get into the ten to twelve anywhere from four to four fifty would be ideal. Um, to get into the six, maybe two two hundred to two twenty five would be ideal. If that is possible.

Crystal clear — $400-450 for 10-12 TH/s, and $200-225 for the 6 TH/s tier. That's really useful for the team to hear.

One thing though — at $400 for 12 TH/s, that's about $33 per terahash. The Avalon Q does 90 TH/s for $1,700, which is roughly $19 per terahash. Way better value per TH. Has something like that ever been on your radar?
It possibly can. Um, what I'm looking for and I haven't looked into this, is what is the power outage on that. I don't wanna be spending a lot of power for a minor lottery play. Cool.

That's exactly the right question — the Avalon Q pulls about 3.5 kilowatts. That's a real bill at home, plus heat and noise. So the lottery miners exist because they're like 50-100 watts — basically free to run.

So when you think about that 12 TH/s sweet spot you described — is the power draw part of why you're hovering right there and not going bigger?

Yes. Um, I just don't wanna again, put in a lot of uh, money into power when and this is strictly a lottery play. If I hit obviously, it's worth it. If I don't, I don't wanna be sinking a lot of money in power just to waste it. So short answer, yes. I'm willing to go up a little higher but I don't wanna spend too much power above the twelve terahash, ten terahash.

Perfect — so power draw is the actual ceiling, not hashrate. The 10-12 TH/s sweet spot is really "the most lottery odds I can buy without my electric bill noticing."

That's a really clean way to think about it. Has anyone else in your life pushed back on you running these — like a partner asking about the electric bill — or is that purely your own internal limit?
I think the nerd ox twelve to or the six terahash would probably be ideal. Only because the Nexus s one is so much more expensive.
Right — Nexus pricing knocks it out. So between the NerdQaxe 6 TH and the NerdOctaxe 12 TH — which way are you actually leaning right now?

Because of the terahash and the price, is actually cheaper to run a twelve terahash being that it's a hundred and forty watts at four sixty nine opposed to buying two six terahashes at two forty nine each, which is more expensive and the power is eighty watts, which is, again, a lot high not a lot higher, but higher electricity. So long story short story, I mean, is uh, go with the twelve terra ash, I believe.

That's a really tight piece of math — you've actually run the watts side by side: 140W for one 12 TH unit vs 160W combined for two 6 TH units, AND it's cheaper upfront. So the Octaxe wins on both axes for you.

Where'd you do that comparison — was that on HD's site directly, or were you cross-referencing somewhere else?
No. I was doing it right on HD. It, uh, states it very clearly

Good to hear — that the specs are clear enough on the page to actually do the math right there. That's not always the case on competitor sites.

Speaking of — when you were shopping around, did you check anywhere else besides HD?
No.
Just HD — okay. What made you skip the comparison shopping this time? Like, you mentioned earlier you've bought Bitmain secondhand and Ice River before — so you know other places exist.
I'm not looking for full scale minor. I'm just looking for a lottery place. And watching the Hobbyist Minors video, it intrigued me.

Got it — Hobbyist Miner videos basically pre-qualified HD for you. You watched, you trusted, you came straight here.

Do you remember anything specific he said about HD — like, did he vouch for them, show shipping, do an unboxing?
He vouch for them. He did say it was free shipping. And he did do an unboxing.

Vouched for them, free shipping, unboxing — that's basically the trifecta. So you arrived already past the "is this legit" question that stops most first-timers cold.

One last thing I want to ask about — the page has this little banner here. Let me point it out. Do you know what this means — "Free return shipping & RMA"?
No. I don't.

Fair — RMA is industry jargon. It stands for "Return Merchandise Authorization" — basically if your unit shows up dead or breaks under warranty, HD pays return shipping and swaps it. Does knowing that change anything for you, or were you already comfortable buying without understanding it?
It, uh, reinforces my purchase to use HD. I really like that the customer service and warranty aspect of it. Where it's a no brainer, and I'm not fighting to get my miners back up and running.

That's huge to hear — "no-brainer, not fighting to get my miners back up." That's exactly the feeling HD is trying to deliver. Have you been burned somewhere else fighting for a return or warranty before? Is that why it lands so hard for you?

No. It's it has not. Uh, just very important. I hear horror stories of other people trying to get warranty it actually hit me once with Ice River, but it wasn't the ASIC. It was actually the power supply that they didn't stand behind. And I had to pay um, the shipping. They they did stand behind the power supply, but not the shipping, which cost me another hundred hundred dollars US in shipping.

There it is — Ice River made you eat $100 in shipping on a power supply RMA. So even though the part was covered, that hundred bucks stuck with you. That's exactly why "free return shipping" lands so hard on the HD page — you've literally paid that bill before.

Where do you hear the horror stories from — Reddit, YouTube comments, Discord?

I've heard it from Reddit A lot of people complaining specifically now about Bitmain. Uh, some YouTube comments that people are having problems with returns and other companies. Standing behind their products I just don't wanna deal with that kind of avenue.

So Reddit and YouTube comments are doing real work — Bitmain horror stories on Reddit specifically are shaping how you think about every other vendor. And HD's free-return-shipping is basically the antidote to the exact thing that burned you on Ice River.

This has been incredibly helpful — really detailed. Before we wrap, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had, or anything you want the HD team to hear directly?

Um, I would like to know if there is a bundle package that has two nerd QXs at six terahash. Um, is there a bundle where it'll come in cheaper than the nerd octa axe twelve terahash? I'm not sure if that is even a bundle, But like I said before, if it is and I can save a little bit of money, employing two of them instead of one, I'm definitely interested. But if not, then I think my mind would be made up with the nerd octa x twelve terahash, and I wanna combine it with a Nexus l one. And, again, I'm not sure if there's a bundle for those two as well. That would save me some money.

Crystal clear — two asks for the team:

One, a bundle of two NerdQaxe 6 TH units priced below the single Octaxe 12 TH.

Two, a NerdOctaxe 12 TH + Nexus S1 combo bundle with a discount.

I'll make sure both of those land with the founders directly — that's exactly the kind of concrete product feedback they're hoping to get from these calls.

Thank you so much, Ari — this was genuinely one of the more detailed conversations I've had. Your $75 discount code will land in your inbox shortly. Have a wonderful day.
Thank you.
Take care.
